equity_bridge.note: FY2025 NCI profit share GBP 2.7m at ~13x; book value GBP 16.4m at 30 June 2026

equity_bridge.item: Remaining transformation cash costs, after tax
equity_bridge.note: GBP 80m programme less 9.9 (FY2024) + 24.9 (FY2025) + 17.5 (H1 FY2026) = ~27.7 remaining, at 25% tax relief

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management organic sales framework (3-6% CAGR 2026-2028), cross-checked to revenue_5yr_cagr; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (+6.6%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (+4.1%) and adjusted EPS (-3.6%): FY2020 equity predates most of the ~GBP 627m placing that funded Iberchem and the 2022 PTIC disposal gain, so book-value growth is capital raised and a one-off gain, not compounding. The 3-year figures are all measured off the FY2022 peak (COVID lipid sales, customer overordering) and are trough-vs-peak artefacts.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs use ADJUSTED basic EPS (FY2020 175.5p, FY2022 272.0p, FY2025 146.2p); IFRS EPS is distorted by the FY2022 disposal gain (464.8p) and FY2025 exceptionals (44.4p). FCF CAGRs are on the owner series (OCF less capex less the share-based payment charge; FY2022 uses the GBP 12.7m equity-statement charge because the cash-flow line was a negative GBP 11.0m settlement movement): FY2020 161.7, FY2022 143.1, FY2025 161.6. SBC is ~0.3% of sales, so owner and reported FCF growth are effectively identical. Owner FCF has been flat for five years on revenue up 22%: the margin collapse (adjusted operating margin 23.0% in FY2020 to 17.4% in FY2025) absorbed all of the acquired growth.

scenario_narratives.base: The three-year plan lands mostly, a year late. Consumer Care keeps growing as global beauty brands return to innovation spend (Beauty Actives +19% in H1 FY2026, ceramides +44%), Pharma Ingredients grows steadily while project-driven Pharma Solutions stays lumpy, and Crop and Industrial Specialties are flat. Reported sales grow ~4-4.5% through FY2030 and fade to 3%. The ~GBP 100m transformation programme delivers most of its savings (GBP 46m banked by June 2026) but part is reinvested or passed on in price, so the adjusted operating margin reaches ~19.6% in FY2028 rather than the >20% target and matures near 21% -- about three points below the pre-2020 level, reflecting a lower-margin F&F mix and an asset base whose depreciation has risen from 4% to 6% of sales. Capex holds at the guided ~6% of sales.
scenario_narratives.bull: Innovation-led recovery in full: New & Protected Products keep outgrowing the group, global brands and regional challengers both grow, lipid and adjuvant platforms in Pharma fill the capacity built in 2021-24 (the assets impaired in FY2025 prove under-earning, not stranded), and Crop restocks. Sales compound at the top of the 3-6% range through FY2030. Operating leverage on an already-invested footprint plus the full GBP 100m of savings takes the adjusted operating margin through 20% in FY2028 and back to ~23% by the early 2030s, close to the pre-2020 franchise margin, with the GBP 50m working-capital release delivered.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2023-24 pattern repeats in milder form. The H1 FY2026 strength turns out to include Middle-East-driven pre-buying and a restock, beauty brands destock again, Asian and biotech-based competitors compress price/mix in Beauty Care and Home Care, and Pharma Solutions capacity stays underused, prompting further impairments. Sales grow 2-2.5%, roughly inflation. Transformation savings are competed away, leaving the adjusted operating margin stuck at ~18% -- above the FY2024 trough but never near the 20% target -- and return on invested capital stays below the 10% goal. The market pays a cyclical-chemicals exit multiple (15x cap) rather than a quality-compounder one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Croda is valued as a recovering quality franchise on mid-cycle adjusted earnings, not on depressed IFRS profit and not on the FY2021-22 peak. The base case gives management credit for most, not all, of its FY2028 framework. The share price has rallied to its 52-week high and already discounts a margin recovery at or beyond the bull path; on house assumptions the stock offers no margin of safety, and the 15% hurdle entry price is a long way below the market.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path is the dominant driver: each 1pp of mature EBITDA margin moves base value by roughly 5%. The >20% FY2028 operating-margin target is a management ambition following a period of missed ambitions.

Trough-vs-peak ambiguity: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA margin (23.3%) is ~5pp below FY2017-19 and ~6pp below FY2021-22. If the pre-2020 margin is the true mid-cycle level the base case is too low; if COVID-era pricing never returns and F&F dilutes the mix, it is about right.

Exceptional items are recurring in practice (GBP 149.5m FY2025, GBP 22.6m H1 FY2026). Only the remaining transformation cash cost is charged; further restructuring beyond the GBP 80m programme would be a direct deduction.
Right-of-use depreciation is assumed (~GBP 17m), not read from a filing; a different figure shifts cash-tax EBIT by a few GBP m only.
Pension surplus (GBP 75m post-tax) excluded; the triennial valuation due in H2 FY2026 could change cash contributions either way.
Sterling: ~65% of translation exposure is USD and EUR, about GBP 1m of adjusted operating profit per cent on each. Projections are in reported GBP at roughly current rates.
The 5 November 2026 Q3 sales update is not in the research corpus and is not reflected.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of, quoted in GBp; 52-week range 2488-3856
data_sources.financials: CRDA.L_Metrics.csv and kpis (FY2014-FY2025, H1 FY2026); CRDA.L_Annual_FY2025.txt (cash flow table lines 655-700, framework lines 431-462); CRDA.L_HalfYear_FY2026.txt (results for six months to 30 June 2026: balance sheet, cash flow, net debt note 7, tax and capex guidance); CRDA.L_Quarterly_Q1-2026.txt
data_sources.qualitative: Company outlook and financial framework statements in the FY2025 annual results and H1 FY2026 interim; no Analysis JSON existed at build time

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted diluted count implied by the H1 FY2026 income statement (adjusted profit attributable GBP 109.5m / diluted adjusted EPS 78.4p = 139.7m; basic 139.3m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the employee share trust buys shares in the market (GBP 7.3m in FY2025) to settle awards.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' add-back GBP 5.0m (CRDA.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:678); no separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). Model -> quote conversion is the fixed 100 pence per pound, not a market FX rate, so it cannot go stale. Magnitude check: adjusted basic EPS FY2025 146.2p against a four-digit pence price gives a mid-20s P/E, confirming the quote is pence.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10-year gilt ~4.5% risk-free, ~5% equity risk premium, beta ~0.95 for a defensive specialty-ingredients name gives cost of equity ~9.3%; pre-tax debt cost ~4.5% (USPP fixed-rate notes) at ~10% debt weight gives WACC ~8.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality and execution risk are charged in the flows and the weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full cash lease payment (FY2025 principal GBP 18.1m + interest GBP 2.8m = GBP 20.9m, 1.2% of sales) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities of GBP 79.4m are EXCLUDED from net debt (company-reported net debt of GBP 577.9m includes them; 577.9 - 79.4 = 498.5). da_pct_path is D&A excluding right-of-use depreciation and excluding amortisation of acquired intangibles. Right-of-use depreciation is not separately printed in the extracted text and is ASSUMED equal to lease principal (~GBP 17m).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; non-controlling interests (profit share GBP 2.7m FY2025, book GBP 16.4m) are deducted once in the equity bridge at ~13x earnings.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with the adaptations for GBp quote, IFRS 16 leases (treatment B), NCI and a near-SBC-zero market. FRESH BUILD, no prior DCF. MID-CYCLE FRAMING: FY2025 is a trough-ish base, not a peak. IFRS operating profit (GBP 110.1m) carries GBP 149.5m of exceptional items (GBP 107.3m impairments, transformation costs, an onerous contract) plus GBP 35.7m acquired-intangible amortisation; the build starts from the company's ADJUSTED EBITDA (GBP 396.6m, 23.3% of sales) and neither extrapolates the FY2021-22 COVID-lipid/overordering peak (adjusted EBITDA margin 29%) nor the FY2024 trough (23.2%). EBITDA BASIS: Croda's adjusted EBITDA is already AFTER the IFRS 2 share-based payment charge, so ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA grossed up by SBC (+0.3pp) and SBC is then deducted on its own line -- charged once, kept visible. OWNER FCF BASE: reported_fcf is the company's own free cash flow (GBP 161.6m: OCF 286.5 less net capex 108.2, lease principal 18.1, plus interest received 3.0, other -1.6) which is AFTER GBP 24.9m of transformation cash costs and AFTER GBP 25.3m interest paid, i.e. a levered figure; the engine's projected flows are unlevered, so year-1 projected FCF sits above last_fcf by roughly the after-tax interest and exceptional cash. Interest income is not stripped (net debt, not net cash). BALANCE SHEET: net debt and cash from the 30 June 2026 interim; using June rather than December net debt is slightly conservative (~35p/share) because the H1 dividend has left the balance sheet while the full FY2026 flow is still in year 1. PENSION: the IAS 19 net surplus (GBP 100.9m pre-tax, GBP 75.4m post-tax) is NOT added -- a UK defined-benefit surplus is not distributable to shareholders on demand; adding it in full would be worth ~54p/share. TRANSFORMATION: GBP 80m total cash cost programme, GBP 52.3m spent to June 2026; the remaining ~GBP 27.7m is deducted after tax in the equity bridge rather than depressing the margin path. BUYBACKS: no buyback programme; the GBP 7.3m is employee-trust purchases that fund the flat count. GAP: the Q3 sales update scheduled for 5 November 2026 is not in the Extracted corpus; year-1 growth rests on H1 FY2026 (reported +2.9%, organic +4.6%, Q2 organic +8.8%) and the unchanged FY2026 outlook. The price is at the top of its 52-week range (2488-3856).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 is reported GBP growth: organic ~5% (H1 +4.6%, Q2 +8.8%, guidance 3-6%) less ~1.5pp currency translation. Years 2-5 sit at the middle of the 3-6% framework, fading to 3%.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA pre-SBC. FY2025 actual 23.6% (23.3% + 0.3 SBC); H1 FY2026 23.9%. Path implies an adjusted operating margin of ~17.9% in FY2026 and ~19.6% in FY2028 -- a deliberate haircut to the >20% FY2028 target, which is reached a year late -- maturing at ~21%, well short of the 24-25% earned before 2020 because the portfolio now carries Fragrances & Flavours and a heavier asset base.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax paid ran 19-22% of adjusted operating profit in FY2023-25 against a guided 26% adjusted effective rate; ramp from 23% to the guided 26% as transformation deductions end.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: inventories + receivables - payables = ~27% of sales, so growth consumes cash. -20% gives partial credit for the targeted ~GBP 50m structural working-capital release by FY2028.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the previous medium-term ambitions were missed by a wide margin (adjusted operating profit fell 46% from FY2022 to FY2024 and GBP 107m of assets were impaired in FY2025), so a plan that again falls short has real precedent; there is no balance-sheet stress (leverage 1.4x) so it goes no higher. Base 50%: guidance has been held through three updates in 2026 and GBP 46m of savings are already delivered. Bull cut to 25%: it needs top-of-range growth AND a return to near-pre-2020 margins AND filled pharma capacity, three largely independent things.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
